transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-17
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 51 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Javier Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CTO, Harbor), Ethan Shaw (Platform), Ravi Desai (Security)

Summary:
- Kickoff to map resilience scenarios for Harbor's user-facing inference endpoints.
- Primary concerns: regional outages, partial degradation (low-latency short responses), and data residency for logs.
- Agreed POC: 48hr pilot in us-west-2 with multi-region fallback to us-east-1, run benchmarks and collect tail latency and error-mode behavior.

Topics:
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
- Fallback policies, traffic steering, and canary rollouts
- SLAs, audit logs, encryption (KMS), and SSO/SAML

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll go for about 50 minutes, quick intros — i'm maya your a-e from Redwood, javier is our se who does the heavy lifting on topology and perf.
[00:18] Priya Nair: thanks maya, priya here, CTO at Harbor. quick context we run realtime recommender endpoints, 99th percentile matters a lot, also we have regulatory reqs for sql engine logs retention.
[00:32] Javier Ortega: hi all, great to meet you. curious about your traffic curve — priya, is this global multi-region today or single region?
[00:41] Priya Nair: mostly us-west today, some eu traffic routed via CDN. goal is multi-region for both latency and DR within 9 months.
[00:50] Ethan Shaw: our peak is around 8k rps across inference endpoints, but bursty — we do lots of small prompts and then longer LLM chains occasionally.
[01:04] Ravi Desai: hi, i'm ravi — security architect. our checklist: SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS for keys, audit logs stored in our vault for seven years. also curious how redwood handles logs in private deployments.
[01:18] Maya Chen: great, that helps. high-level: redwood has three modes — hosted api (fastest to start), dedicated reserved pools (predictable throughput), and private vpc/on-prem for strict compliance. each has different tradeoffs for routing and fallbacks.
[01:35] Speaker 1: (mumble) and one more thing is, with hosted we do have region steering and can do a primary/secondary region policy, but for private you manage networking.
[01:47] Priya Nair: can you walk through a failure scenario — say a zone or region goes down, how does your fallback matrix work?
[01:56] Javier Ortega: absolutely. typical policy: hotpath routing — keep primary in region A, if latency spikes above a threshold or API errors exceed x% we re-route to a secondary region or fall back to a smaller quantized model. we also have circuit breakers to avoid cascading failures.
[02:17] Ethan Shaw: quantify 'above threshold'—is that per-route or global? what about cold-start KV cache misses?
[02:26] Javier Ortega: thresholds can be per-route or per-model. we support prefix/KV cache strategies; on cache miss you'll see higher tail latency but the routing policy can prefer a warm standby instance to serve hotprefix. the runtime also supports continuous batching but that must be tuned to preserve p95/p99 SLO.
[02:45] Priya Nair: does that mean in low-cost fallback mode responses are truncated or we return shorter completions?
[02:52] Maya Chen: yes — we call that graceful degradation: you can configure model variants and truncation policies. for example, during outage you can prefer a cheaper quantized 8-bit variant that returns shorter summaries to preserve availability.
[03:07] Ravi Desai: how do you handle data residency and logs in hosted? we can't have logs leave eu for some customers.
[03:15] Maya Chen: hosted has region-specific logging and retention controls; for strict residency you would typically go dedicated with VPC peering or private where customer-managed logging and KMS is enforced.
[03:27] Ethan Shaw: any SLOs for hosted region failover? like time to detect and switch?
[03:33] Javier Ortega: detection is based on health checks and metrics. typical failover detection is 30-120s depending on sensitivity, then plus DNS/route convergence ~ a few secs if proxied, longer if using BGP. we can also use active health probes and traffic mirroring for canary rollouts to validate fallback.
[03:53] Priya Nair: in your latency numbers i saw p99 around 800ms, but we need <500ms for interactive widgets. can dedicated help?
[04:02] Maya Chen: dedicated gives predictable hardware pinning and reserved capacity; you can hit lower p99 with right GPU class and low-concurrency lanes. also local region placement reduces network variance.
[04:16] Ethan Shaw: what's the cost delta roughly between hosted and dedicated?
[04:20] Maya Chen: varies a lot, quick rule: hosted pure pay-as-you-go will be higher per-token but you avoid infra management. dedicated requires commit but unit cost can be 30-60% lower depending on utilization and batching. we'll share a cost-model spreadsheet.
[04:34] Ravi Desai: security: does redwood support customer-managed KMS in hosted?
[04:39] Javier Ortega: hosted supports BYOK integrations with major cloud KMS, yes. for private you bring your own HSM if you need. audit logs can be streamed to your SIEM.
[04:50] Priya Nair: ok re: fallback — curious about partial degradation: if model latency causes 10% of tokens to miss, do you return degraded responses or an error?
[04:59] Javier Ortega: configurable. options: fail open (serve shorter result), fail closed (return error/503), or queue for longer latency. we recommend fail open with graceful truncation for customer-facing widgets.
[05:14] Speaker 2: (crosstalk) what about model state and kv cache consistency across regions?
[05:20] Javier Ortega: good Q. cross-region KV replication has latency cost; for low-latency you can keep separate warms per-region and rely on eventual consistency, or use async replication for non-critical cache entries. if you need strict consistency, private deployment with your own storage is recommended.
[05:39] Ethan Shaw: for our recommender chains we rely on short lived KV per session; losing warm cache on failover will increase latency dramatically — what's your approach?
[05:49] Javier Ortega: we can pin sessions to a region as long as the region is healthy; on failover there are strategies: session sticky routing with a transfer plan (best-effort), or transparent rehydration using a central session store. each has tradeoffs.
[06:05] Priya Nair: what is the typical outage scenario coverage in your SLA for dedicated customers?
[06:12] Maya Chen: dedicated SLA focuses on uptime of the reserved pool and latency targets; we provide credits for sustained breaches. exact terms depend on contract tier. for hosted we publish region uptime and we have multi-region agrmt for enterprise.
[06:26] Ravi Desai: can we get the legal redlines up front — especially around data deletion, e-discovery and logging?
[06:33] Maya Chen: yes we'll send the security + legal pack. also javier can discuss our audit log retention and deletion hooks.
[06:42] Speaker 1: (mumble) something about routing tiers and canary rules..
[06:47] Javier Ortega: canary rules let you send a fraction of traffic to a new model or region. we support percentage routing and header-based steering (e.g., VIPs or geos). automatic rollback can trigger on error rate or latency regressions.
[06:59] Ethan Shaw: in practice how fast do you recommend failing back to a previous model? if we flip quickly we might thrash.
[07:07] Javier Ortega: we add cooldown windows and circuit-breaker thresholds to prevent thrashing. also buffer queues during transient spikes.
[07:17] Priya Nair: i'd like a clear fallback matrix document — for region outage, for model crash, for latency degradation, for KV inconsistency — with recommended behaviors.
[07:25] Maya Chen: noted, we'll provide a fallback matrix template and fill it for your topology as part of the pilot.
[07:33] Speaker 2: (static) are there any open-source bits we need to run for private?
[07:38] Javier Ortega: private includes our runtime package and an operator for your k8s clusters; we provide a helm chart and install guide. no large open-source changes needed.
[07:48] Ethan Shaw: about the pilot — what telemetry do you need from our side?
[07:53] Javier Ortega: sample traffic profile, priority routes, any synthetic tests you want run, and credentials to a dev VPC (read-only) for test harness.
[08:01] Priya Nair: timeline — we want to decide by end of q4, pilot this month if possible.
[08:07] Maya Chen: sounds doable; we can spin up a pilot in us-west-2 and a failover us-east-1 standby. javier will prepare config.
[08:16] Ravi Desai: one more security nit — how are model artifacts handled in dedicated vs hosted? are weights ever stored unencrypted?
[08:24] Javier Ortega: weights are stored encrypted at rest; in hosted we manage encryption with customer KMS integration if you enable BYOK. in private obviously you control storage lifecycle.
[08:35] Priya Nair: what about auditability — can we get per-request tracing and token-level cost attribution?
[08:42] Maya Chen: yes our console provides token-level breakdowns, per-route traces, and tracing hooks to export to your tracing backend. we also include request IDs in logs for correlation.
[08:55] Ethan Shaw: ok let's talk about the actual fallback behaviors we want in pilot: prefer warm standby, degrade to shorter completions, and only route to quantized variant if latency > 1.2s, otherwise keep full model.
[09:08] Javier Ortega: that's straightforward. we'll parameterize thresholds and include cooldowns.
[09:16] Priya Nair: curious if redwood can simulate chaos, like a region blackhole during pilot?
[09:22] Maya Chen: we can coordinate a controlled failover test. javier can script a simulated region outage by blocking egress and measuring traffic steering.
[09:31] Ethan Shaw: perfect. that will validate our app behavior.
[09:36] Speaker 1: (overlap) any blockers on compliance for you?
[09:39] Ravi Desai: main blockers: log residency, ability to rotate keys, and contractual liability limits around PII.
[09:46] Maya Chen: we will include rotation procedures and sample clauses.
[09:50] Priya Nair: ok next steps?
[09:52] Maya Chen: recap: maya will send security pack and pricing; javier will prepare pilot config and runbook; ethan to send traffic profile; set pilot window 2027-09-22 to 2027-09-24. follow-up on 2027-10-01 to review.
[10:10] Ethan Shaw: noted. thanks all.
[10:13] Priya Nair: thanks everyone.
[10:16] Maya Chen: thanks — bye.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker label switches and minor word substitutions (e.g., 'K-V cash' for KV cache). references shared: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack, https://redwood.example.com/pilot-runbook, cost-model spreadsheet link (shared live).

End of transcript.
file_notes: Pilot scoped as 48hr on us-west-2 with failover to us-east-1; fallback matrix and security pack to be shared. Caller had strict log residency requirement; recommended dedicated or private for EU-stored logs.
